analyst_view.overall: Early view: Las Palmas are on their third coach, Albert Sánchez, appointed on 29 October; he won 3-2 at Oviedo in his first game and then drew 0-0 with Eldense. Andorra are 18th and in an emotional position after their goalkeeper Jesús Owono was involved in the collision that killed Tenerife's Jesús de Miguel; their 8 November game with Mallorca was postponed at the club's request. The bans listed for Owono, Lautaro De León and Efe Akman should be served at Almería on 14 November.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean lower: Las Palmas' home games have averaged about two goals, and the 0-0 against Eldense showed a side still learning Sánchez's ideas. Andorra's away games are more open, which stops me going much lower.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners. I lean lower: Las Palmas won only four corners against Eldense despite 61% possession, and Andorra under Carles Manso keep the ball (74% at Tenerife) but took just three corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.1 cards. I lean higher: Andorra are among the most-booked sides in the division (40 yellows and two reds in 12 games), with Diego Alende, Marc Domènech and Akman all on five or more yellows.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.0 shots. I lean lower: Las Palmas took nine shots against Eldense and Andorra 11 at Tenerife even with most of the ball, so neither side generates big volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. I lean lower: Las Palmas had three on target against Eldense and Andorra four at Tenerife.
